_comment: Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/AcidParting/tools/make_shape.py. Native frame, block units, controller cell at [0,0,0]: the front cell at ground level, where the fire door and the ash mouth are. One porcelain vessel in a sand bath over a small fire, under a brick hood open in front; vessels stand side by side in a row along x (up to parting.rowMax), sharing one chimney on one member's outlet, the others capped. No power and no forced air: natural draught, in at the ash mouth (ash, ashSide) under the damper, the fuel in at the fire door (firedoor, firedoorSide). depth is the fire door: 0 open, slid up in its guides (the rest pose), 1 shut. theta is the stoker's clock, carried by a ratio-0 rotate on the door: nothing turns. requires: the build's stages, brickwork (with the hoodiron part), lining and fittings (the bath, vessel, tub, siphon and door parts) (build; the frame, iron, has none); the damper's place, damperopen, damperhalf or dampershut (one at a time); the fire, fuel (laid) or fire (burning); the vessel's contents: charge (granulated dore), acid, solution (the silver dissolved), gold (the parted gold), wash (the wash water, poured in from a bucket); the tub's: copper (the copper plates on their rod), liquor (the drawn-off solution), silver (the silver sludge); and outletcap. The brickwork's texture is the brick type's (bricks). vesselCell, vesselFace: the hood's cell, the vessel worked through its open front (vessel: its mouth, where the gold comes out); tubCell, tubFace: the same cell and face, the precipitating tub at its front (tub: its mouth, the silver's hand-draw point): a click there is the nearer of vessel and tub's. No water anchor: the vessel is watered from a bucket, at the vessel. outletCell: the stack's head, in the back row, the chimney stood on its top; chimney: the shortest chimney, counted from the outlet up. See AcidParting/README.md.

build._comment: The build's stages, in order (a proposal for the owner but for the counts measured from the model). frame: the iron frame's grid recipe (with a hammer); placing it puts down the controller and its ghosts, and draws the frame part. Each stage then fits its requires when its materials are all in: brickwork (its alsoParts, the hood's lintel, comes with it at no cost of its own), then lining, then fittings (its parts: the sand bath with its sand, the vessel, the precipitating tub and its siphon, and the fire door; also: the damper, in one of its places). volumeBlocks: the stage's brick measured from the model, in blocks; its quantities are that at 2 fired bricks or 4 refractory bricks a block (the game's brick block recipes), rounded up, fire clay one per 2.5 refractory bricks. perClick stack: a click puts in as many of the held stack as are still needed. oneType: the first fired brick put in sets the brick type (bricks), and the rest must match. The parting vessel's own item is open (the game has no porcelain vessel). The tub's copper plates are contents (copper), put in by hand and worn away. No water line: the wash water is poured in from a bucket. outletCap: an item interaction, not a stage.

bricks._comment: The fired brick types the brickwork takes (every game:burnedbrick type), each with the block its bricks make and that block's texture: the renderer sets the shape's 'brick' code to the vessel's type's base, with its overlays drawn over it (the crucible furnace's table). The type is the first brick put in; until then no brick is drawn.

parting._comment: minChimney: chimney blocks stood on the outlet, counted from it up (the crucible furnace's MinChimneyHeight); rowMax, rowAxis: vessels in a row, side by side along x, sharing one chimney.
